summary.headline: Krishival Foods H1 FY27 revenue rose 50% to INR174.62 crores and EBITDA 63% to INR24.56 crores, with Q2 revenue up 28% to INR85.66 crores.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR85.66 crores (up 28% YoY), EBITDA rose 53% to INR13.87 crores at a 16.6% margin, and PAT grew 18% to INR6.82 crores. Ice cream revenue grew about 65% to INR22.50 crores with EBITDA of INR3.53 crores and a 16% margin, while the nuts and dry fruits division grew 19% to INR63.16 crores. Management reiterated FY27 targets of about 50% top-line and 50% profit growth and a INR1,500 crore consolidated revenue target for FY29. Management said the company was carrying inventory build-up and receivables rise, which it attributed to festive-season timing, ice cream sales tripling and input-cost hedging.

financial_highlights.metric: Nuts and dry fruits revenue (Q2 FY27)
Nuts and dry fruits EBITDA (Q2 FY27)

segments.name: Nuts, dry fruits and healthy snacks (Krishival Nuts)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR63.16 crores (+19% YoY), EBITDA INR10.44 crores (+33%), margin 17%. Management guided 20-25% growth for the next two to three quarters and a 15-16% EBITDA target; B2B (mithai ingredient partners) is about 55% and B2C about 45% of mix, per the analyst.

segments.name: Ice cream and desserts (Melt N Mellow)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR22.50 crores (about +65% YoY), EBITDA INR3.53 crores at 16% margin versus an 8% internal target; Q1 ice cream EBITDA margin was 10.25%. Deep freezers at 18,752 against a 27,000 target for FY27-end; 35,000+ retail touchpoints; 205 distributors after adding 85 in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target of about 50% top-line growth and about 50% profit growth, which management said it is on course for given H1 growth of 50% revenue and 63% EBITDA.
Nuts growth expected at 20-25% over the next two to three quarters; ice cream growth expected to be roughly double the nuts growth.
Ice cream capacity utilisation to reach about 37% this financial year, with full utilisation targeted in Q1 FY29, which management said can deliver INR600 crores of ice cream top line.
Nuts and dry fruits and ice cream expected to reach a 50:50 revenue split by March 2028.
FY29 described as the inflection point for net profit, with a consolidated revenue target of INR1,500 crores; depreciation expected to rise modestly from deep-freezer expansion.
Borrowings to rise in ice cream next financial year; no further borrowing expected in nuts for 1-1.5 years.
capex_capacity: Nuts: 10 MT per day finished kernel capacity added in May 2026, taking total to 20 MT per day; target 40 MT per day by FY28 (management said by March 2028); only about 25% of the added capacity expected to be utilised this financial year.
Ice cream: Sambhajinagar plant installed capacity 1 lakh litres per day, plus 20 MT per day milk products and 10 MT per day bakery; about 37% utilisation expected this year.
Deep freezers: 18,752 at end Q2 FY27, target 27,000 by FY27-end; network runs through 13 depots.
Mellow & Co. FOCO retail: first outlet at Apte Road, Pune (about 1,400 sq ft carpet area) under commissioning, with launch expected shortly; plan of 15 to 25 outlets in Pune as spokes.
demand_pricing: Ice cream expanded into Andhra Pradesh and then Tamil Nadu (Vellore, Hosur, Erode, Tiruvannamalai, Salem) in Q2; 80-85% of sales expected from Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
Management said no further state expansion is planned until ice cream top line reaches INR600 crores; any future territory would be Kerala, Odisha or Chhattisgarh.
Ice cream seasonality: July-August slack, so about INR55 crores of the INR85 crores Q2 sales came in September.
Nuts B2C share in the last six months rose to about 20% (e-commerce, modern trade) from 5-7% last year, per management.
Singapore exports: USD384,000 shipment in Q2; about 300 retail touchpoints in Singapore. US and Japan being explored, with US distribution targeted within about two years.
Competition: management said Melt N Mellow is the only Indian ice cream player it knows of that has built EBITDA-positive general trade expansion across more than five states since March 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why are nuts growing only 15-20% and why is nuts EBITDA margin so high (about 70% per analyst)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nuts growth was 15-20% over the last three to four quarters, with 20-25% expected in the next two to three quarters. It attributed margin strength to sourcing and inventory management, B2B mithai-partner pricing, and a 14-16% EBITDA range maintained for about two years; 15-16% is the target and anything above is a bonus.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables and inventories rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 sales were front-loaded into September (about INR55 crores of INR85 crores) on festive and ice cream timing, plus a rise in B2C/e-commerce mix. Inventory build was a deliberate buffer against El Nino, drought, oil and input inflation. It called receivables transient, with March the low point for nuts.

qa_highlights.question: How will competition from a large player entering affordable ice cream affect Melt N Mellow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has solved general trade, is EBITDA-positive since March 2026, and has experience handling competitors, so new entrants would not stall growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale for the FOCO model for Mellow & Co. outlets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said franchisee-operated outlets risk brand dilution, so the company keeps operations in-house while franchisees fund rent and electricity. This gives an asset-light model, with gross margins about double regular retail, and the existing 200-plus field staff can run the stores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for depreciation, interest and net profit margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation rises this year from deep-freezer expansion but should not jump much after that; management said FY29 is the net-profit inflection point, tied to the INR1,500 crore revenue target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable borrowing level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said borrowing will increase only in ice cream next year, balanced by EBITDA and top-line growth; nuts will not need further debt for one to 1.5 years.

risks_watch: Input-cost inflation (El Nino, sugar, crude oil, nut prices) and whether margin gains hold in H2 FY27; management said it expects no profitability hit over the next six months.
Working capital: receivables and inventory rose sharply in H1; watch the March 2027 balance and the reversal of the inventory build.
Borrowings rising in ice cream to fund expansion; watch the debt level against EBITDA.
Competitive entry in ice cream from a large player at affordable price points, and the pace of general-trade expansion into Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.
Execution risk on the 20-to-40 MT nuts capacity ramp and the 27,000 deep-freezer target; depreciation and finance cost pressure from the expansion.
Mellow & Co. outlet launch in Pune and the 15-25 FOCO outlet rollout.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on H1 growth and margins, with repeated emphasis on sourcing and cost control. Less specific and somewhat evasive on the drivers of the receivables and inventory rise, on the nuts margin ceiling, and on the timing of the export and US expansion. Several answers were loosely structured, and some figures (such as the EBITDA margin basis and the 70% margin) were not clearly reconciled.
key_quotes: Our focus is on offering products across different price points, strengthening our brands, and expanding our distribution reach to address a wider consumer base.
While scaling, we strongly believe the scaling has to be with profit.
So therefore ice cream is witnessing a very -- almost double the growth of the nut segment.

adds.what: 10 MT/day finished kernel capacity added in nuts (May 2026), taking total to 20 MT/day
Nuts capacity to 40 MT/day finished kernel by FY28 (target)
Deep freezers: 18,752 at end Q2 FY27, target 27,000 by FY27-end
Mellow & Co. FOCO retail outlet at Apte Road, Pune (about 1,400 sq ft) with 15-25 Pune outlets planned

growth.why: Management reiterated about 50% FY27 top-line and profit growth, backed by H1 revenue +50% and EBITDA +63%, with ice cream capacity utilisation rising to about 37% this year, a 10 MT/day nuts capacity addition already live and a 40 MT/day nuts target by FY28, but nuts growth is guided only at 20-25% and the ice cream and nuts capacity targets lack firm order or contract backing.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Nuts EBITDA margin at 17% in Q2 against a 15-16% target, and ice cream margin at 16% versus an 8% FY27 guide, but management said the nuts margin is above target and expects no profitability hit over the next six months; input-cost inflation (El Nino, sugar, crude, nuts) is a live risk.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: The 10 MT/day nuts kernel addition went live in May 2026 (total 20 MT/day), and deep freezers are rising from 18,752 toward a 27,000 target at FY27-end (44% added so far), with the first Mellow & Co. outlet in Pune under commissioning.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guided nuts growth of 20-25% for the next two to three quarters and ice cream growth roughly double nuts, with Q2 ice cream revenue up about 65% and H1 up roughly 3x.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Nuts utilisation is low (only about 25% of the added 10 MT/day expected to be used this year), but ice cream is at about 37% utilisation this year with a 40 MT/day nuts target by FY28, so further capex is guided rather than firmly dated; a new plant announcement is not clearly signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue rose 50% and EBITDA 63%, management reiterated about 50% FY27 top-line and profit growth and said it is on course, but nuts growth is guided only at 20-25% and receivables and inventory rose sharply, so a formal raise is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivables and inventory build in H1 (Q2 sales front-loaded with about INR55 crores of INR85 crores in September) and input-cost risks could pressure cash and margins, and the nuts EBITDA target was cut to 15-16%, though management reiterated its FY27 targets.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Mellow & Co. FOCO first outlet at Apte Road, Pune (about 1,400 sq ft) is under commissioning with launch expected shortly, and the plan is 15-25 Pune outlets over time.

rows.label: Ice cream general-trade expansion into Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu; Singapore
rows.why: Ice cream expanded into AP and Tamil Nadu in Q2 with about 300 Singapore retail touchpoints and a USD384,000 Q2 shipment, but management said no further state expansion until ice cream top line reaches INR600 crores, and US distribution is targeted within about two years.

rows.label: Borrowings rise in ice cream next year; nuts debt-free for 1-1.5 years
rows.why: Management said borrowing will rise in ice cream next year to fund the deep-freezer expansion, while no further nuts borrowing is expected for 1-1.5 years.

rows.label: Reversal of H1 inventory and receivables build
rows.why: Receivables and inventory rose sharply in H1 on festive timing and an El Nino buffer; management called receivables transient with March the low point, but the reversal is not yet shown in numbers.

tone.note: Management was confident on H1 growth (revenue +50%, EBITDA +63%) and on ice cream expansion, but cautious and loosely structured on the receivables and inventory build, the nuts margin ceiling and export timing; analysts pressed on the high nuts EBITDA margin (about 70% per analyst) and working cap
